'''GSS-TSIG (Generic Security Service Algorithm for Secret Key Transaction)''' is an extension to the [[TSIG]] DNS [[authentication protocol]] for secure key exchange. It is a GSS-API algorithm which uses [[Kerberos (protocol)|Kerberos]] for passing security tokens to provide authentication, integrity and confidentiality.  

GSS-TSIG (RFC 3645) uses a mechanism like [[SPNEGO]] with [[Kerberos (protocol)|Kerberos]] or [[NTLM]]. In Windows, this implementation is called ''Secure Dynamic Update''.<ref>[https://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/library/cc961412.aspx Secure Dynamic Update: Windows 2000 DNS - MSDN]</ref>

GSS-TSIG uses [[TKEY record]]s for key exchange between the DNS client and server in GSS-TSIG mode. For authentication between the DNS client and [[Active Directory]], the AS-REQ, AS-REP, TGS-REQ, TGS-REP exchanges must take place for granting of ticket and establishing a security context. The security context has a limited lifetime during which dynamic updates to the DNS server can take place.
